(BY SHRI VISHAL SANOTHIYA - G.A.)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER 1.

This is 4th bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of regular bail in connection with FIR No.15/2020 dated 6.11.2020 registered at P.S - Crime Branch, Indore District - Indore for offences punishable under Section(s) 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B, 34 of IPC.
2.
The third bail application was already rejected on merit vide order dated 17/1/2022 passed in M.Cr.C No.53268/2021.
3. Against the order, the applicant filed Special Leave to Appeal(Criminal) No.1374/2022.
The said Special Leave petition was dismissed by granting liberty to the applicant to renew the prayer for bail after reasonable time, if there is any change of circumstances.

4. As per the prosecution case, the raid was conducted at a call center and it was found that a racket was being operated by which the accused persons used to call the foreign citizens of the USA and to blackmail them saying that they are involved in criminal cases and threatened them for cancellation Mehul Patil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101027075/
1 of social security and will disclose the number to the authorities and they will be implicated in criminal cases.

sentences.text: They had taken huge amount in Dollars.
The role of the applicant is attributed as a closure that he used to convert the foreign currency into Indian currency along with co-accused Karan Bhati and main accused Ravi Rami.
5. Counsel for the applicant submits that after the order passed by the Apex Court, 9 months have passed.
There are 23 accused persons.
18 accused persons have been granted bail and one has died.
The trial is likely to take time and therefore, he be enlarged on bail.

6 . Counsel for the State opposes the prayer for grant of bail on the ground that the bail application of the applicant has already been dismissed on merits and against the said order SLP was filed, which has also been dismissed and the liberty was granted to renew the prayer after reasonable time if there is any change of circumstances.
He further submits that there is no change of circumstances.

It is argued that the accused persons who were callers of the call centers have been granted bail by this Court but none of the persons whose role was of closure and converting foreign currency into Indian currency has been granted bail.
It is further submitted that recently one of the co-accused Karan Bhati has been arrested and there are 287 call details with the Karan Bhati.
The main accused Ravi Rami is still absconding.
He further submits that the voice sample of the applicant has been sent to the FSL and the same has been verified as voice of the applicant with the call details of foreign citizens.
The statement of foreign citizens has been recorded through video conferencing and they have made allegation of fraud and cheating with them.
FBI has also submitted its report and as per the report, 13 Crore Dollars which is approximately Rs.1000 Crore has been cheated from the foreign citizens by the racket operating in India.
Counsel submits that there is one similar case against the applicant of the year 2018 and he is a habitual offender.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the role attributed to the present applicant and that the voice sample of the applicant has been verified and 287 call details with recently arrested co-accused Karan Bhati and the main accused Ravi Rami is yet to be arrested, the foreign citizens have been cheated and a huge amount of 13 Crore Dollars i.e. about Rs.1000 Crores involved in the present case.
Apart from that, there is one similar case against the applicant.
The earlier bail application was also dismissed on merit and there is no change in circumstances, therefore, I do not find any case for grant of bail.
M.Cr.C. is accordingly dismissed.

(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) JUDGE Pramod Mehul Patil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101027075/
